Theme

Latin word

trādō

trādō, trādere, trādidī, trāditum

verb, third conjugation

hand over, hand (to someone); introduce, recommend (a person to someone)

In this lexicon

  • give

    also used · classical · Gell. 15.17.1: trāditās sibi tībiās

  • introduce

    the recommended word · classical · Cic. Fam. 7.5.3: tōtum dēnique hominem tibi ita trādō; Hor. Epist. 1.9.3: ut tibi sē laudāre et trādere cōner; Traupman 16–17, 334

Examples

  • tōtum dēnique hominem tibi ita trādō, dē manū, ut ajunt, in manum tuam istam et victōriā et fidē praestantem

    In short, I hand the whole man over to you, from my hand, as they say, into that hand of yours, so outstanding in victory and in good faith.Cic. Fam. 7.5.3

    In the entry for introduce

  • Septimius, Claudī, nīmīrum intellegit ūnus, quantī mē faciās, nam cum rogat et prece cōgit scīlicet ut tibi sē laudāre et trādere cōner

    Septimius, Claudius, is plainly the only one who knows how much you think of me: for he asks, and begs me, if you please, to try to commend and introduce him to you.Hor. Epist. 1.9.1–3

    In the entry for introduce

  • ego autem ā patre ita eram dēductus ad Scaevolam sūmptā virīlī togā, ut, quoad possem et licēret, ā senis latere numquam discēderem

    When I had put on the toga of manhood, my father took me to Scaevola, and so, as far as I could and was allowed, I never left the old man’s side.Cic. Amic. 1
